message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"6.26","text":"While I was discussing these things with Appion, Peter arrived from Caesarea, and crowds converged in Tyre, hurrying to meet him and thank him for coming. Appion withdrew with only Anubion and Athenodorus, but all the rest of us set out to meet Peter. I was the first to welcome him in front of the gates, and I led him to the lodging. When we arrived there, we dismissed the crowds. When he asked me to tell him what had happened, I held nothing back; instead, I reported Simon’s slanders, the monstrous apparitions he had produced, how many illnesses he had sent after the feast arising from the ox sacrifice, and that, of those who were ill, some had remained right there in Tyre, while the others had gone away with Simon to Sidon at the same time as my arrival, in expectation of being healed by him. I also reported that I had learned that none of them had obtained healing from him, and I recounted to Peter the discussion I had had with Appion. Then, to show affection and offer encouragement, he praised and blessed me. After partaking of salt, because of the exertions of the journey, he gave himself over to the most necessary rest of sleep.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συνδρομαὶ τῶν ὄχλων","chosen":"crowds converged","rationale":"The phrase describes crowds running or gathering together, not merely static assemblies."},{"source_quote":"χάριν τῇ ἐπιδημίᾳ ὁμολογεῖν","chosen":"thank him for coming","rationale":"ἐπιδημία can denote an arrival, presence, or visit; the immediate context favors Peter’s coming to Tyre."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τὴν ξενίαν","chosen":"to the lodging","rationale":"ξενία may denote hospitality or guest quarters; here it functions as the destination where Peter would stay."},{"source_quote":"τὰς τερατώδεις φαντασίας ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γεγενημένας","chosen":"the monstrous apparitions he had produced","rationale":"φαντασίαι can be appearances, apparitions, or illusions; “apparitions” preserves their presented visual character without deciding whether they were real or deceptive."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὅσας ἔπεμψεν νόσους","chosen":"how many illnesses he had sent","rationale":"ὅσας preserves the emphasis on their number or extent; it could also be rendered “all the illnesses that he had sent.”"},{"source_quote":"μετὰ τὴν ἐκ τῆς βουθυσίας ἑστίασιν","chosen":"after the feast arising from the ox sacrifice","rationale":"βουθυσία is an ox sacrifice, while ἐκ presents the feast as proceeding from or resulting from it; “the feast from/of the ox sacrifice” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"ἅμα τῷ ἐμὲ ἐλθεῖν","chosen":"at the same time as my arrival","rationale":"The construction expresses simultaneity; the alternative “as soon as I arrived” would give it a stronger sequential force."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ θεραπευθησόμενοι","chosen":"in expectation of being healed by him","rationale":"ὡς with the future participle presents the travelers’ purpose or expectation rather than endorsing the expected healing as fact."},{"source_quote":"στοργῆς καὶ προτροπῆς χάριν","chosen":"to show affection and offer encouragement","rationale":"χάριν marks the purpose of Peter’s praise and blessing; προτροπή may also be rendered “exhortation.”"},{"source_quote":"ἁλῶν μεταλαβών","chosen":"after partaking of salt","rationale":"The translation preserves the explicit salt image; the phrase may contextually imply sharing or eating food more generally."},{"source_quote":"τῇ ἀναγκαιοτάτῃ ἡσυχίᾳ τοῦ ὕπνου ἑαυτὸν ἐπέτρεπεν","chosen":"he gave himself over to the most necessary rest of sleep","rationale":"This retains the superlative force of ἀναγκαιοτάτῃ and the image of entrusting or yielding oneself to sleep."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
